newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-AVALANCHE WIN AGAIN WITH BEST PLAYERS SIDELINED.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-AVALANCHE WIN AGAIN WITH BEST PLAYERS SIDELINED.

text.p: Even with their best players sidelined by injuries, the defending Stanley Cup champion Colorado Avalanche keep finding ways to win.
Adam Deadmarsh scored with 1:31 left and Patrick Roy made 37 saves as the Avalanche extended their unbeaten streak to 10 games with a 3-2 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs.
Deadmarsh, who has six goals and three assists during the streak, took a drop pass from Sandis Ozolinsh and fired a wrist shot from the top of the slot that beat Felix Potvin.
Deadmarsh said Ozolinsh "made the whole play happen. He came up with a great deal of speed and backed those (defensemen) off. And he just dropped it back to me."
Colorado is 7-0-3 in its last 10 and became the first team to reach 60 points despite playing without top stars Joe Sakic and Peter Forsberg as well as Valeri Kamensky and Mike Ricci.
Keith Jones and Ozolinsh had powerplay goals for Colorado. Kirk Muller and Todd Warriner scored for the Leafs, who suffered their fourth straight loss.
"Considering our situation, struggling for a playoff spot ... it's not what we need," said Larry Murphy, who set up both Toronto goals.
In Montreal, the surging Canadiens scored on their first four shots of the second period and held on for a 6-3 victory over the Boston Bruins.
Mark Recchi tallied twice for his second consecutive two-goal game and Stephane Richer added a goal and two assists for the Canadiens, who are 5-1-3 in their last nine games.
Boston goalie Bob Tallas surrendered four goals on only eight shots before being pulled in favour of Tim Cheveldae.
Ray Bourque had a pair of powerplay goals for Boston.
In Detroit, Ed Belfour turned aside 33 shots and Tony Amonte had a goal and an assist as the Chicago Blackhawks beat the Red Wings 3-1.
Belfour held the Red Wings scoreless for the first 54 minutes to snap his 10-game winless streak (0-6-4). The victory was his first since November 30.
James Black and Bob Probert also scored for Chicago.
Brendan Shanahan spoiled Belfour's shutout bid with a powerplay tally at 14:41 of the third.
In Ottawa, Stu Barnes scored at 6:41 of the third period to help the Pittsburgh Penguins extend their unbeaten string to 11 games with a 3-3 tie against the Senators.
Patrick Lalime stopped 31 shots for Pittsburgh, improving to 11-0-2 since he was called up from the minors.

Lalime made a huge save on Daniel Alfredsson's shot from the slot in the final minute of regulation to preserve the tie. "No question, he stole the game for us," Penguins coach Ed Johnston said Lalime. "He continues to amaze me."
In Philadelphia, Rod Brind'Amour's goal with 43 seconds left in regulation lifted the Flyers into a 3-3 tie with the Washington Capitals.

With goaltender Garth Snow pulled for an extra attacker, the Flyers swarmed the Capitals net. Goalie Olaf Kolzig stopped a slap shot by Eric Desjardins, but the puck came loose in the crease and Brind'Amour was able to tap it in.
The Caps took advantage of a pair of two-man advantages in the second period to take a 3-1 lead.
In Calgary, Ray Sheppard and Radek Dvorak each had a goal and an assist and John Vanbiesbrouck stopped 40 shots as the Florida Panthers shut down the Flames 4-1.
Tom Fitzgerald and Bill Lindsay scored the other goals for the Panthers, who won for only the second time in seven games.
Aaron Gavey was the only one to get past Vanbiesbrouck, scoring the lone Flames goal at 10:28 of the first after Florida had jumped out to a 2-0 lead.
In Edmonton, Vlastimil Kroupa scored on the power play with 9:08 left to give the San Jose Sharks a 2-1 win over the Oilers.
Kroupa was at the left point when he took a feed from Todd Gill and blasted the puck past Marty McSorley's screen and through goaltender Curtis Joseph's pads for the game-winner.
Edmonton's Miroslav Satan scored a powerplay goal 38 seconds into the second period, but Al Iafrate tallied with 4:31 to go in the period to tie the game.
At Tampa Bay, Igor Ulanov's drove home a slap shot from the left point midway through the third period to lift the Lightning into a 4-4 tie with the New York Islanders.
The Lightning erased a two-goal deficit in the third period on a goal by John Cullen at 3:46 and Ulanov's tally to extend their unbeaten streak to four games.
Travis Green and Zigmund Palffy each had a goal and an assist for the Isles, who halted a five-game losing streak but have just one win in their last 10 games.
In Los Angeles, Dimitri Khristich scored with 33 seconds to play to give the Kings a 2-1 win over the St Louis Blues.
Khristich skated into the high slot and unloaded a slap shot that beat Grant Fuhr to the glove side for his third goal in two games.
Kevin Stevens scored the first Kings goal on a power play with just 12 seconds left in the first period. Brett Hull accounted for the Blues' offence with a powerplay tally in the second period.
Byron Dafoe made 27 saves for the Kings.
